title: adaptive-presubmit-weighting-and-dep-erosion-audit
author: Priya Anand
description: Motivation: Our presubmit lanes are increasingly costly and noisy — historic data shows a small set of flakes and a handful of transitive dependency churn cause disproportionate CI load and developer context switches. This PR introduces two orthogonal improvements: 1) adaptive presubmit weighting: presubmit shards/lint lanes are assigned dynamic weights driven by a short-term historical failure rate and cost model so flakiest, highest-cost checks are deprioritized to fast feedback lanes; 2) dependency-erosion audit: a lightweight tool that scans dependency graphs across workspace modules and flags packages that are losing reverse-deps over time (an early warning for erosion and accidental breakage), surfaced as a check and a Prometheus metric. Implementation summary: - Add a presubmit weighting controller that reads historical failure metrics from CI telemetry and outputs weights into ci/presubmit/weights.json; the controller is implemented as scripts/ci/measure-flakiness.py and a small service wrapper in tools/presubmit-weighter/main.go. - Introduce tools/dep-erosion (Go) which traverses the module graph (go mod graph + yarn/npm for JS workspaces) and compares snapshots stored in ci/dep-snapshots/ to compute erosion score and produces SARIF-compatible results and a Prometheus metric (ci_dep_erosion_score). - Wire the weighting into .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml: a pre-step fetches weights and adjusts job matrix sizes and fastpath lanes. The default policy is conservative (only affects non-blocking lint shards for the first week). - Add docs: docs/ci/presubmit-weighting.md and an entry in docs/release-notes/2024-06-presubmit-weighting.md. Rollout plan: - Stage 0: dry-run for one week (weights computed and logged, no change in job selection). - Stage 1: enable adaptive weighting for non-blocking lint shards on main for 10% of PRs for 48h. - Stage 2: increase to 50% and add JS/TS lint lanes if metrics stable. - Stage 3: full rollout with safeguards and automatic rollback on >5% increase in median wall-time or >3% failure rate delta. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of weighter and erosion scanner - [x] Unit tests for weighter logic and scanner heuristics - [x] Prometheus metrics + Grafana basic dashboard panels - [x] Docs + runbook entry for rollback - [x] Canary rollout plan and Linear tickets listed in description Changes & intent: This PR is primarily CI configuration and tools; it aims to lower aggregate CI wall-time and reduce developer cost. It deliberately does not change blocking test selection for the first 30 days. See linked Linear items for product decision notes.

review_comments: Asha Patel: Nice direction. Two asks before approving: 1) add a sanity cap so a single flaky check can't reduce other shards below a minimum capacity; 2) can we make the dep-erosion scanner run in < 2m for monorepo scale?

Priya Anand: Reply: Added a min_shard_capacity config and optimized the scanner by parallelizing module graph snapshots; receipts in commit h7i8j9k. Erosion scanner time reduced to ~95s in our perf run on staging.
Miguel Torres: Please make the weights.json schema explicit and add a validation step in CI to avoid malformed weight inflight. Also add a feature flag to disable adaptive weighting per-repo.
Priya Anand: Reply: Added JSON schema and validation in CI; feature flag introduced via repo-level labels and .github/ci-flags.yaml. Updated docs.
Linnea Karlsson: Approved after minor nits. Verified metrics on staging; no regression in median latency.
ci_log_summary: Initial run: lint shard failed due to strict schema validation (caught during review). Fixed schema mismatch and a flake in scripts/ci/test_utils. Final run: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, go vet).
release_notes: Adaptive presubmit weighting (conservative rollout) to reduce CI wall-time and a dep-erosion audit tool which surfaces packages losing reverse-deps. No runtime changes to production code. See docs/ci/presubmit-weighting.md for details and rollback procedures.
